items: Ask the group to tell the story from last week.

data.text: Read or watch Matthew 4:12-17 two times as others listen.

data.html:
Jesus Begins to Preach

12 When Jesus heard that John had been put in prison, he withdrew to Galilee.13 Leaving Nazareth, he went and lived in Capernaum, which was by the lake in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali—14 to fulfill what was said through the prophet Isaiah:

15 “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali,
the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan,
Galilee of the Gentiles—
16 the people living in darkness
have seen a great light;
on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned.”

17 From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”

items: What caught your attention or what did you like best? Why?
What is new or has developed at this point in Jesus story?
What do we learn about the humanity or divinity of Jesus from this passage?
How can we live differently now that we know this story?
What is Jesus modeling to us about life and ministry or godly leadership?
Read the story again. Have someone tell the story and ask the group to correct if necessary.

data.text: Jesus now moves into a period of transition in His ministry. At the beginning of this period, John was put in prison and this prompted Jesus to move to north to Galilee. Jesus was then rejected in his home village of Nazareth. He relocates, choosing the city of Capernaum on the lake shore as his new home base. This is a strategic location as it is on a major international highway of that time. Jesus’ fame is growing and spreading. With John the Baptist now in prison, there is a transition of leadership of the Kingdom message. Jesus begins to focus His message to the same message that John had, “repent for the kingdom of heaven is near.”
